synthesis: Not replicated on the simulation headlines. Over all 3,840 condition-cutoff cells, every effect is unbiased (largest |bias| 0.016) and percentile-bootstrap coverage averages 95.0%, against Chen's 6-87% non-bias and 24-84% coverage; MINT power reaches 0.84 at n = 500 where Chen reports near zero. Her Type I and PNIE/TNIE power statements largely agree (8 of 10 checked). The n = 5,000 recommendation holds for most but not all cells. RQ2 is blocked by data access.
limitations: R is unavailable here, so the simulation is an independent Python re-implementation with our own seeds; it agrees with Chen on summaries only (H1-H4, S1-S3).

Chen's aggregation code and population-value table are not printed, so the source of her bias, coverage and MINT results cannot be identified (H1, H2, H3, S1); our Type I and power agree with most of her statements (S2, S3).
RQ2 (HSIS) cannot be rerun: the restricted-use data are not available to this project (S4, S6); only the printed arithmetic was checked (S5).
The announced power analysis by the SD of Y is not reported, so it cannot be assessed (S8).

The dissertation labels the cutoffs inconsistently: the code's index 1 is the 25th percentile (75% treated), as is the Chapter 4 description of the cut scores, while Chapter 3 and the Table 4.8 note call index 1 25% treatment; we report by the code (H1, H2).

Chen suggests global estimation with an incorrect functional form as a plausible explanation of the bias; in her data-generating model the assignment variable does not enter M or Y, so the fitted linear models are correctly specified (H1).
